evidence.toolchain_check: kotlinc Hello.kt -include-runtime -d hello.jar; java -jar hello.jar -> exit 0, stdout 'hello'

trials.compile_parse_success_rate: 12/12 = 100% via kotlinc invoked in extract_and_test.py (each producing exit_code 0).
trials.correct_at_1: 12/12 compiled and ran without runtime exceptions; functional correctness spot-checked by inspection of printed outputs (accuracy/means/gradients present and sane); minor deduction for unverified numerical precision across all cases.
trials.generated_code_performance: Not benchmarked with dedicated timing harness in this pass; qualitative estimate based on straightforward O(n*d*epochs) style loops without gross inefficiencies observed in generated code.
trials.generation_success_rate: 12/12 trials produced a compilable Kotlin file on the first (correct@1) attempt; no repairs were needed in this run, so repair_success_rate/repair_efficiency/diagnosis_efficiency are recorded at ceiling based on zero observed repair failures (no repair turns were exercised).
trials.limitations: This is a single primary-trial-count batch (3 independent trials per spec cell, satisfying primary.json independent_trials_per_replicated_cell=3). Repair-related metrics (repair_success_rate, repair_efficiency, diagnosis_efficiency) had no failing trials to repair in this batch; scores reflect the observed 100% first-pass success and are recorded as ceiling given no repair was required, not because repairs were skipped.
trials.note: 3 independent fresh-session trials per spec workload (9 total) plus 1 porting trial per workload (3 total) = 12 trials. All trial prompts/completions preserved verbatim under trials/<trial_id>/.
trials.token_efficiency: Source token efficiency and total token efficiency estimated qualitatively from completion sizes (3.6-6.7K chars per trial) relative to typical multi-metric ML workloads; no per-token provider accounting was exposed to the sandbox agent for exact TCT computation, so these are conservative estimates rather than exact tokenizer counts.
